content:
John Ternus is taking over as Apple's new CEO this week, and the Financial Times today ran a piece profiling his life and how he is regarded by Apple employees and partners.

Latest profile of Ternus reveals more details about Apple's new CEO

John Ternus officially took over as Apple CEO, with Tim Cook recently transitioning to executive chairman, passing the baton to him.

9to5Mac editor Chance Miller has compiled a detailed breakdown of Ternus's background in a separate article, including his education, early career, past public statements, and more.

However, the new profile published by the Financial Times today adds further details and insights.

Speaking of Ternus's reputation inside Apple, the article said he is "known internally as exceptionally capable and low-key and pragmatic." A senior executive at a major supplier that has worked with Apple for many years echoed this view:

However, a former Apple executive told the Financial Times that Ternus "is relatively less well known outside the hardware division" within the company. However, since the exact timing of that executive's departure from Apple is unclear, Ternus's standing inside the company over the past year appears to have risen significantly.

Cook has said Apple "very much wanted this transition to go as well as possible." And based on a small anecdote in the profile, the transition does appear to have been received positively internally.

Beyond that, the Financial Times also revealed some important details about Ternus's private life. The report notes that he is married with children, and was born and raised in California.

For more on Apple's new CEO, see our previous coverage:

  • Who is John Ternus? Everything you need to know about Apple's next CEO
  • John Ternus makes first appearance as Apple CEO, reveals his priorities
  • Read the full internal memo Ternus sent to Apple employees on his first day as CEO

Apple holds its big iPhone event next week, where we will see Ternus make his first public appearance as CEO.
